clue.text: Ben is considered big in Scotland

definitions.text: Ben is considered big in Scotland

parts.words: Ben is considered big in Scotland
parts.note: a Scottish 'ben' is a mountain, and the biggest of them all is the one Fort William sits beneath

explanation.surface: Someone called Ben enjoys a big reputation north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' looks like a man's name, but in Scotland a ben is a mountain; the highest in Britain is Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's highest peak, in the Scottish Highlands, is the mountain whose second name this is.

clue.text: Bank facility extended to clergyman? That is correct

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a facility a bank provides
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A bank lending to a vicar's assistant is judged to be doing the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extended to' joins the two pieces; 'That is' is a link pointing at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is free from error, which is what being right or correct means.

clue.text: An equally certain guarantee

parts.note: as, in 'as tall as', means to an equal degree
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A promise that is just as dependable as the other one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An equally certain' reads as AS SURE, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to promise it firmly, removing doubt.

clue.text: A record's set in the mountains

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record, so record's gives LP plus the S

explanation.surface: An album is made with mountain scenery as its backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' joins the pieces rather than signalling an insertion: A then LP'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The range across Switzerland, Austria and neighbouring countries is Europe's best-known mountain chain.

clue.text: Cement on a board

parts.note: builders carry their bonding mix on a flat hand-held board named after it, and graduates wear a square cap of the same name

explanation.surface: Building material spread on a flat plank.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonding paste between bricks is carried on a hawk, which builders call by its board name.

clue.text: Normal, square flags

explanation.surface: Ordinary, old-fashioned banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Normal' and 'square' (conventional) both describe what is standard; 'flags' gives the noun sense, banners carried as standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual or conventional, and military standards are banners or flags.

clue.text: Novel chess piece designed in northern city

parts.note: novel means new
the castle is another name for the rook in chess

explanation.surface: A new chess set has been designed in a city in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed in' is a link joining wordplay to definition. NEWCASTLE upon Tyne is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyneside city is the largest in north-east England.

clue.text: May perhaps take thirty-one days

parts.note: May reads as 'might', but it is the calendar period, one of seven with thirty-one days

explanation.surface: Something might well take a full thirty-one days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' at the start hides its capital: it is the fifth calendar period, which does indeed last thirty-one days.
explanation.definitionFit: May is one of the twelve divisions of the calendar year, here one of the longer ones.

clue.text: Bad smell at the royal society when heating is on and soup is served

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
RS stands for the Royal Society, Britain's scientific academy
CH is the abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: An unpleasant whiff at a learned society once the radiators are on and dinner arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at', 'when ... is on and' and 'is served' join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Borsch is the beetroot broth of Russia and Ukraine.

clue.text: Put the boot in? Ooh, you sound like a Kenyan!

indicators.note: the speaker is told how their words come across when spoken, so we hear them rather than read them

parts.words: Put the boot in? Ooh, you
parts.note: to put the boot in is to kick, so this is a cry of 'kick! ooh, you'

explanation.surface: Someone told to kick out is told they sound like a man from Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the boot in' is KICK; said with 'Ooh, you' it sounds like the name of Kenya's largest people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kikuyu are Kenya's largest ethnic group, so one of them is a Kenyan.

clue.text: In hut, sting macho type into having a row

annotationWithheld.why: In hut, sting macho type into having a row: HUT + STING gives a T where SHOUTING has an O, and no reading of 'macho type into' supplies the O; the clue looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: In hut, sting macho type into having a row

clue.text: A skill valued in biblical times

explanation.surface: A gift prized in the days of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible (the parable of the talents) a talent is a large weight of silver or gold, a unit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift or aptitude is a talent, and the ancient talent was a unit of weight used for valuing silver.

clue.text: Name the French bird first

indicators.note: the bird comes first, before the French article

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Put the French name for a bird at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is what a book or film is called, its name.

clue.text: Slaver who brought out African wildcat

indicators.note: letters brought out of their order are shaken into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A slave trader who shipped an African cat abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a link; 'brought out' rearranges SLAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The serval is a long-legged, spotted wild cat of the African savanna.

clue.text: Team gets heated on the subject of whiskers

parts.note: a side is a team
something heated too far burns

explanation.surface: A team grows hot under the collar about facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the subject of' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the cheeks, a kind of facial whiskers.

clue.text: Stay in Scotland, and propose Edinburgh initially

parts.note: to bid is to propose or offer

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Remain in Scotland and make an offer in its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: BIDE is chiefly Scots or old-fashioned for stay or remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bide is a Scots and archaic verb meaning remain or wait, as in 'bide a wee'.

clue.text: Spoil the booze, take the edge off it

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
gin is a type of booze

explanation.surface: Ruin a drink and take away its bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the' and 'off it' are link words around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the border or edge of a page or area.

clue.text: Produced and gave backing to continental dairy product

indicators.note: backing means read from the back, so the cheese name runs right to left

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A farm made a Dutch cheese and supported it.
explanation.definitionFit: Made is the past tense of make, so it means created or produced.

clue.text: Little details of the time one acre was included

indicators.note: the two short pieces are included within the word for a unit of time

parts.note: a minute is a unit of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fine points of the occasion when a small plot was added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. I and A go inside MINUTE, between T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, precise or trivial points.

clue.text: Seller of fruit with oddly dull centre

indicators.note: the fruit is given a new centre made of the odd letters
the fruit is given a new centre made of the odd letters

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of dull

explanation.surface: A market trader of fruit whose middle has gone flavourless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling hawker who sells small goods.

clue.text: Recently put down the telephone in mid-word

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the middle of the word for put down

parts.note: to lay is to put down
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Not long ago someone hung up halfway through speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down the telephone' looks like hanging up; it is two pieces, LAY and TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately means in the recent past, not long ago.

clue.text: The size of former temporary accommodation

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: How big the old camping shelter was.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the area, scale or size of something.

clue.text: Our pet getting confused by actors

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A family pet is bewildered by a group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a touring company of performers such as actors.

clue.text: Pass out in Jaffa international airport

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across Jaffa and international

explanation.surface: Someone collapses at Jaffa's international airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airport' is surface padding left over as a link; the run starts in the last two letters of Jaffa.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to lose consciousness briefly, or pass out.

clue.text: Busy making Victorian skirt?

explanation.surface: Busy sewing a Victorian dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A bustle was a pad or frame worn under the back of a Victorian skirt; making one is jokily 'bustling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustling means full of energetic activity, and the second sense is a whimsical verb from the Victorian dress padding.

clue.text: Thug will continue

explanation.surface: A heavy will keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is GO ON read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a hired heavy or ruffian, and go on means carry on or continue.

clue.text: Expenditure goes beyond deposit

parts.note: out can mean beyond, as in out of range
to lay is to deposit, as a hen lays an egg

explanation.surface: Spending is greater than the money put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlay is money spent, an expense or expenditure.

clue.text: Almost recognise lines of hillock

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: to know someone is to recognise them
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Nearly identifying the contour lines on a small hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill or mound.

clue.text: Expresses dissatisfaction with firm putting motorway on flatlands

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
M is used for motorway, as in the M1
plains are broad stretches of flat land

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a company building a motorway across open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'putting ... on' join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to voice grievance or discontent.
